To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a comparison of 5 methods for the clinical diagnosis of FASD showed that the 4-Item Checklist was the most sensitive and specific method; (2) the 4-ITEM CHECKLIST was the most accurate method for the clinical diagnosis; (3) the 2-ITEM CHECKLIST and the 4- ITEM CHECKLIST were the most sensitive and accurate methods for identifying FAS and ARND; (4) the FASD-DS was the most specific

(a) the 4-item AUDIT-C was the most accurate screening test for detecting heavy drinking, (b) the 4- and 2-item AUDIT-C were the most accurate screening tests for detecting hazardous drinking, (c) the 4-, 3-, and 2-item versions were all accurate screening tests for hazardous drinking among men, and (d) the 4-and 3-item AUDIT-C versions were accurate screening tests for heavy drinking among women.
(a) the FASD-DRS and the FASD-NI are valid and reliable tools that can be used to diagnose FASD, and (b) the FASDS is also a valid and reliable tool that can be used for the diagnosis of FASD.

the development of an efficient method for the clinical diagnosis of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD).
the development of an effective, efficient, and reliable clinical assessment procedure for FASD.
the development of a new method for the diagnosis of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders.

the most reliable method for diagnosis of FASD is a multidisciplinary approach that includes clinical assessment, medical and social history, physical and neurodevelopmental examination, and a thorough review of all available records, such as school reports, medical records, and psychological testing results.
there is a lack of consensus among the experts in the field of FASD regarding the most effective method for the diagnosis of FASD.
there is not yet a reliable and accurate diagnostic method for FASD.

there is no single best method of diagnosis for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD).
we found no single method to be superior to all others for clinical diagnosis of FASD.
there is a great deal of variation in the clinical diagnosis of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) in the literature, and that the variation is related to the method used to make the diagnosis.
